strings.name: Alex Morgan
strings.role: Retired football player and sports investor
strings.summary: Alex Morgan was a forward on two U.S. World Cup-winning teams and the London Olympic gold-medal squad, with club success in America and Europe. Her speed and important goals made her a prominent public figure in women’s football. After retiring in 2024, she continued through her foundation, media and a San Diego Wave investment to expand opportunities for girls.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A World Cup-winning forward, she advances women’s football’s professional development and international public visibility.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: California, United States; raised in Diamond Bar
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: UC Berkeley degree in political economy, 2010
strings.highlights.h1.title: National-team and club titles
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won the 2015 and 2019 World Cups, 2012 Olympic gold and a Champions League with Lyon.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Women’s sport after retirement
strings.highlights.h2.text: Established a foundation and became a Wave minority investor, advancing opportunity and investment.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Wave investment
strings.timeline.t1.text: Became a minority investor in her former club, San Diego Wave.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Final professional match
strings.timeline.t2.text: Announced retirement September 5 and played her Wave farewell September 8.
strings.timeline.t3.title: NWSL Golden Boot
strings.timeline.t3.text: Led regular-season scoring with 15 goals in 17 games.
strings.timeline.t4.title: World Cup retained
strings.timeline.t4.text: Helped the United States win and received the Silver Boot.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Lyon’s Champions League title
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won the Women’s Champions League during her short spell at Lyon.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First World Cup title
strings.timeline.t6.text: Played all seven matches as the United States won.
strings.timeline.t7.title: London Olympic gold
strings.timeline.t7.text: Scored the extra-time semifinal winner against Canada before the team won gold.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Senior international debut
strings.timeline.t8.text: Debuted against Mexico on March 31 and finished her Berkeley studies that year.
